risk_note: RV2 by path (payment, ledger, payout, union, platform). B2-15q made onModuleDestroy wait for the tick in flight, without a limit: a tick stuck in pool.connect() when the PostgreSQL host is lost kept context.close() waiting, handles.close never ran, and docker's SIGKILL came with no log line. Five timers now wait at most TICK_STOP_WAIT_MS 800 ms through waitForTickStop, then log worker_tick_stop_timed_out and return; the bound timer is unref'd and cleared. 800 ms because Nest calls onModuleDestroy module by module (read in @nestjs/core): five timers are at most 4 s. The worst case with queue.stop 5 s and handles.close 5 s is 14 s, over docker's 10 s, so a hard stop can still be SIGKILLed, but the warn is out by then and it never waits longer than before. Nine other unbounded waits (listed in the ledger) are not covered. No global deadline, because staging's stop_grace_period is 30 s.
